# Yeast substitution groups
# status: DRAFT. Written from general brewing knowledge as relationships between named strains. Not copied from, and not
# verified against, the reference sites; spot-check lines against them and flip the last column to `reviewed`.
# compare against: BeerMaverick yeast substitutions chart, Jay's Brewing yeast substitution list
# (both blocked to scripts; open in a browser)
#
# line format: id | members (separated by ;) | tier | what changes | review
# tier: close = near drop-in | fair = same style family, noticeable difference | distant = last resort | never = do NOT swap
# Strain codes are included so a search for US-05, WLP001, 1056 or M44 hits the line. Dry versus liquid is a handling
# difference, not a strain difference; a dry strain that shares a lineage is listed as close/fair. Always compare
# fermentation temperature range and flocculation before accepting, and check BF yeast data for attenuation.
# Search with: grep -i "<name or code>" knowledge/yeast.md
#
Y-US-ALE | Safale US-05; US-05; US05; Fermentis US-05; Wyeast 1056; WY1056; American Ale; WLP001; California Ale; White Labs WLP001; BRY-97; LalBrew BRY-97; Mangrove Jack's M44; US West Coast; M44; Imperial A07 Flagship; CellarScience Cali | close | clean, neutral American ale; attenuation 78-82%; M44 and BRY-97 are slightly drier and cleaner, WLP001 and 1056 are the liquid lineage | draft
Y-US-ALE-NEUTRAL | US-05; Nottingham; LalBrew Nottingham; LalBrew House Ale; House Ale; Pinnacle American Ale; Pinnacle Heritage American Ale; Heritage American Ale | fair | neutral, clean ale strains; Nottingham is very clean and flocculates well; Pinnacle American Ale is described by the shop as a neutral American ale strain, check its product sheet | draft
Y-ENGLISH | Safale S-04; S-04; Windsor; LalBrew Windsor; WLP002; English Ale; Wyeast 1968; London ESB; Mangrove Jack's M07; Pinnacle English Ale; Pinnacle Heritage English Ale; Wyeast 1099; WLP007; Imperial A09 | fair | fruity, low attenuation, high flocculation; S-04 is the most attenuative of the dry options, Windsor leaves more body and esters | draft
Y-NEIPA | LalBrew New England; Verdant IPA; LalBrew Verdant; Pomona IPA; LalBrew Pomona; Pinnacle Juicy IPA; WLP066; London Fog; Wyeast 1318; London Ale III; CellarScience NE Hazy; CellarScience Jungle; Imperial A38 Juice; Mangrove Jack's M66; Hophead; Mangrove Jack's Hophead | fair | juicy, low flocculation and often highly attenuative ale strains for hazy IPAs; Verdant and 1318 are English lineage with stone-fruit esters, M66 and Jungle are hop-forward biotransformation strains | draft
Y-LAGER-GERMAN | SafLager W-34/70; W-34/70; W34/70; Wyeast 2124; WLP830; German Lager; Weihenstephan; LalBrew Diamond; Imperial L13 | close | the standard clean German lager; ferment cool (9-14 C), very reliable | draft
Y-LAGER-DRY | SafLager W-34/70; SafLager S-23; S-23; LalBrew NovaLager; NovaLager; SafLager S-189; SafLager SH-45; E-30; Pinnacle Pilsner; Pinnacle Lager | fair | dry lager yeasts; S-23 is a touch fruitier, NovaLager is clean and fast, S-189 is the Swiss, ultra-clean option | draft
Y-WHEAT | Safbrew WB-06; WB-06; Safale WB-06; Safale W-68; W-68; LalBrew Munich Classic; Munich Classic; Wyeast 3068; Weihenstephan Weizen; WLP300; Mangrove Jack's M20; Bavarian Wheat; CellarScience Hefe; Imperial B44 | fair | banana and clove hefeweizen character; WB-06, W-68 and M20 are the usual dry choices (W-68 is the classic Weihenstephan-style wheat strain) and give more clove, Munich Classic is milder; low flocculation, cloudy beer | draft
Y-BOTTLE | LalBrew CBC-1; CBC-1; Cask and Bottle Conditioning yeast; Bottle conditioning yeast; Safale US-05; Safale S-04 | fair | CBC-1 is made for re-fermenting in bottle and cask, ferments well in high alcohol; a small pinch of a neutral ale yeast also works for ordinary beers | draft
Y-LOWALC | Safbrew LA-01; LA-01; Low alcohol yeast; Safale US-05; Safale S-04 | never | LA-01 is a special low-alcohol yeast that leaves maltose unfermented; ordinary ale yeast would give full-strength beer | draft
Y-BELGIAN | Safbrew T-58; T-58; Safbrew BE-256; BE-256; Safale S-33; S-33; LalBrew Abbaye; Abbaye; Mangrove Jack's M41; Belgian Ale; WLP530; WLP500; Wyeast 3787; Wyeast 1214 | fair | spicy and fruity Belgian and abbey ale; T-58 is spicy and peppery, Abbaye is more fruity, BE-256 is more attenuative, S-33 is a general-purpose Belgian-origin ale strain | draft
Y-SAISON | Safbrew BE-134; BE-134; Mangrove Jack's M29; French Saison; CellarScience Maison; Wyeast 3711; WLP565; WLP566; WLP568; Saison | fair | very dry and peppery; BE-134, M29 and Maison are strongly attenuative and ferment warm; Wyeast 3711 is the dry-finishing French strain | draft
Y-KVEIK | LalBrew Voss Kveik; Voss; Kveik Yeastery Eitrheim; Eitrheim; Kveik Yeastery Ebbegarden; Ebbegarden; Kveik Yeastery Stalljen; Stalljen; CellarScience Røkkar; CellarScience Rokkar; CellarScience Velo; Kveik | fair | Norwegian farmhouse and clean high-temp strains that tolerate warm fermentation and finish fast; Voss is orange-like, Velo is very clean across a wide range, Eitrheim is fruity; check the temperature range | draft
Y-SOUR-PHILLY | WildBrew Philly Sour; Philly Sour; Lachancea; Pinnacle Crisp Sour | fair | single-strain lactic acid producers used in one step; acidity level and fermentation temperature differ, check the product notes | draft
Y-SOUR-BLEND | Sour Pitch; WildBrew Sour Pitch; Lactobacillus; Lacto; Lallemand Sour Pitch | distant | lactobacillus-based blends acidify before or alongside yeast and behave differently from a Lachancea single strain; do not swap one-for-one without rethinking the process | draft
Y-ALE-SAFALE-GENERIC | Safale US-05; Safale S-04; Safale K-97; K-97; Safale T-58; Safale S-33 | fair | Fermentis ale family; K-97 is a clean-to-lightly-fruity German ale strain for altbier, kölsch and some wheats | draft
Y-CIDER | SafCider AS-2; Fermentis SafCider AS-2; SafCider AB-1; Mangrove Jack's M02; Mangrove Jack's Sidra M08; M08; Browin Ciderini; Sidra raugs; Cider yeast | fair | apple-focused strains; some are more fruit-preserving and others ferment completely dry; check the sweetness goal | draft
Y-WINE-WHITE | Lalvin D47; ICV-D47; Lalvin QA23; QA23; Lalvin K1-V1116; K1-V1116; Lalvin R2; R2; Vinoferm Chardonnay; Chardonnay; Ziedu Vīniem | fair | white, floral and rosé wine strains; D47 and R2 are aromatic, QA23 is clean and low-foam, K1-V1116 is a robust, fast fermenter | draft
Y-WINE-RED | Lalvin RC212; Bourgovin RC212; RC212; Lalvin Bourgovin | close | red wine strain that favours colour and fruit; if no other is available, compare alcohol tolerance and temperature with a general-purpose wine strain | draft
Y-WINE-CHAMPAGNE | Lalvin EC-1118; EC-1118; Prise de Mousse; Vinoferm Champ; Champ; Fermentis SafCider AS-2; Champagne yeast | fair | very robust, neutral, alcohol tolerant; good for restarting stuck ferments and high gravity | draft
Y-MEAD | Lalvin D47; ICV-D47; Mangrove Jack's M05; Medus raugs; Mead yeast; Vinoferm Mead; Medalus raugs; Enovini Honey; Browin Medalus | fair | mead strains; D47 leaves a bit of honey character, M05 is drier and cleaner | draft
Y-DRY-LIQUID | White Labs WLP001; Wyeast 1056; Safale US-05 | close | same lineage in liquid and dry form; liquid needs a starter or fresh packs, dry is pitched directly | draft
Y-DISTILLERS | Turbo; Turbo Yeast; Pinnacle Distillers Yeast; Distillers Yeast; Koji | never | distilling and turbo yeasts are not for beer or wine; they leave off-flavours and are not substitutes | draft
Y-WINE-BEER-NEVER | Wine yeast; Lalvin; Vinoferm; Beer yeast; Safale; SafLager | never | wine yeast is not a normal substitute for beer yeast: it ferments out, lacks flocculation and gives the wrong flavour; allow only in a strong beer-style cider or mead | draft
